what_happened: Job 20261026-145124-ssmw ("Run defaults proposals automatically after introspection and at drain") failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 1 of 3 the critic said the reading misread the request. The reading assumed that automatically created defaults proposals within the limit would "go through drain's existing steward path". No such path exists. `propose` writes DefaultsProposal records. Drain's approval path only works on steward WorkItems of kind Proposal, read through `split_open` and `open_proposals` from `records.work_items`. Nothing turns a defaults proposal into a work item. The critic gave one major finding: the plan's criterion 4 test stubs `queue()` to release fake Waiting items after `propose` is called, so it passes whether or not a real proposal reaches drain. It gave two minor findings: the drain-stub half of criterion 2 is vacuous, and `auto_propose` would print "no class has repeated..." after every introspection and at every drain start. It gave one nit: deleting defaults.toml to make propose fail may also break introspection or config loading. The introspection hook itself and criteria 1, 3 and 5 were judged sound. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Nothing checks a reading's claims about existing code paths against the code before the plan is built. The reading named "drain's existing steward path" as the destination for defaults proposals without confirming that the two record types (DefaultsProposal and steward WorkItem) are connected. The critic is the first stage to open drain.rs and work_decisions.rs, and it gets only three rounds and keeps no partial plan, so the gap stops the job. The planner also writes a stub-based demonstration that cannot fail, since it proves the stub and not the behavior. The request left the approval route for defaults proposals unstated, and nothing makes the reading name that route and where it exists today.
prevention: Add a required step to the reading stage: for every existing path, record type, role or function the reading says a feature will use, it must cite the file and line where it exists in the current snapshot, and for each hand-off between components it must name the record type that crosses it. Where no bridge exists, the reading must list building it as a deliverable or flag it as an open question to the user. The reading is checked against the code, for example by a cheap pre-critic pass that resolves every cited symbol, before planning starts. Demonstrations for hand-off criteria must run through the real component (here RealSteps), not a stub.
proposed_request: Run defaults proposals automatically after introspection and at drain. Outcome: after each introspection settles, and once at the start of each drain, Athena runs the defaults proposal step on its own, so repeated failure classes produce proposals without the operator running `athena propose`. Today `propose` writes DefaultsProposal records, but drain's approval path (RealSteps::queue, work_decisions::split_open, open_proposals) reads only steward WorkItems of kind Proposal, so defaults proposals never reach it. Build a real bridge, so an in-limit defaults proposal becomes an approvable item in drain and an over-limit one waits for the owner. Acceptance: (1) after an introspection finishes, any defaults proposal that is due is created, and a failure in the proposal step never fails the introspection; (2) at drain start the same step runs once; (3) `athena status` lists open defaults proposals; (4) a test using RealSteps and real records shows an in-limit defaults proposal reaching drain's approve path and an over-limit one staying waiting, with a control that fails when the bridge is removed; (5) when nothing is due, the automatic path prints nothing; (6) a test makes the proposal step fail without touching defaults.toml and shows introspection still completes. Deliverables may include introspect.rs, proposals.rs, drain.rs, work_decisions.rs, status.rs, reading.rs and tests/introspection.rs.
